chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū Ḥamzah, who said:
I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying:

Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام is a door that Allah opened. So whoever enters it is a believer, and whoever exits from it is a disbeliever, and whoever neither enters it nor exits from it is among the class concerning whom Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said:
For Me, concerning them, is the decision.

key_terms.الطَّبَقَةِ: a class or category of people
key_terms.الْمَشِيئَةُ: the divine will or decision concerning their final state
key_terms.بَابٌ: a gate or door signifying an appointed point of entry
key_terms.فَتَحَهُ اللَّهُ: opened by Allah; divinely established and authorized
key_terms.كَافِرًا: a disbeliever, one who rejects and departs from the truth
key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا: a believer, one counted among the people of iman

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام being the door opened by Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the wilayah of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as a divinely opened gate that distinguishes belief from disbelief. It also mentions a third group who remain suspended under Allah’s mashi'ah, indicating a category whose final outcome is left to the divine decision.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Hamza who said,

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> is a door which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Opened. So the one who enters it would be a Momin, and the one who exits from it would be a disbeliever, and the one who does not enter it and does not exit from it would be in the layer (under a category about) which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High has Said:
‘For Me<sup>azwj</sup>, regarding them, is the (pending) decision’.
